metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets The Philippines

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 creative thinking results for the Philippines using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically applies sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for each participating country/economy. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used for variance estimation, so the precise weighting implementation cannot be verified from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported uncertainty statements (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicate that standard PISA variance estimation procedures were used, but the specific weight/replicate details are not included in this excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing PISA 2022 creative thinking performance and related associations; it does not provide an analysis pipeline that specifies plausible-value (PV) generation/combining rules or missing-data handling for an empirical model estimated by the authors. The reported results are descriptive/benchmark comparisons (means, proficiency shares, relative success, and correlations/variance explained) rather than a student-level ML model with documented PV and missing-data procedures. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not reported in the provided text, and extracting them would require the underlying OECD technical documentation not included here.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample for the Philippines consists of 7,193 students in 188 schools who completed the PISA 2022 creative thinking assessment (reported here alongside mathematics, reading, or science completion). The factsheet does not describe additional exclusions beyond the requirement that students completed the relevant PISA assessment components used for the reported creative thinking results.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet reports PISA 2022 Creative Thinking results for 15-year-old students in the Philippines. It summarizes overall creative thinking proficiency on a 60-point scale, proficiency levels (baseline Level 3 and top Levels 5–6), and relative performance compared with the OECD average and selected comparison countries/economies. The test measures three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving), with scoring based on human judgement using rubrics. The factsheet also highlights within-country gaps by socio-economic quartiles and gender, and reports associations between creative thinking and students’ beliefs/attitudes, as well as school environment and digital activity patterns. Methodological caveats are noted for countries/economies with sampling-standard issues (asterisks), but the provided excerpt does not specify the exact weighting, PV, or missing-data procedures used in the underlying OECD database computations.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet that summarizes descriptive and benchmark statistics rather than presenting an original empirical ML study with a documented predictive pipeline. As a result, there is no model training/evaluation, no ML algorithm comparison, and no target-variable-specific predictive findings to tabulate in the main_findings structure. The extraction therefore leaves ML-related fields empty and focuses on the assessment design and reported descriptive outcomes.
